mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals improving labor market conditions, which increases consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 20-day windows following a UNRATE decline, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 4% indicates tighter monetary policy, which may reduce corporate borrowing and consumer spending, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 50% of the 60-day windows following a FEDFUNDS increase above 4%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP (GDPC1) growth accelerates and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases, it signals a strong economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 30% of the 20-day windows following concurrent GDP growth and UNRATE decline, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates increased economic activity, which may lead to higher corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 20-day windows following an INDPRO increase, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in housing starts (HOUST) indicates increased construction activity and economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 50% of the 60-day windows following a HOUST increase, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) is rising, it indicates inflationary pressures that may negatively impact corporate margins and lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 40% of the 60-day windows following the trigger conditions, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) by more than 100,000 jobs indicates a strong labor market, which may lead to increased consumer spending and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 30% of the 20-day windows following a PAYEMS increase, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in retail sales (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer demand, which may lead to higher corporate revenues and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 50% of the 60-day windows following an RSAFS increase, the hypothesis is rejected.
